4	---
5	
6	# pcb-design
7	
8	This skill guides an agent through a KiCad board design. The agent designs and edits the circuit.
9	The script `scripts/pcb.py` checks the project and runs the tools. The script never designs a circuit.
10	
11	## Scope
12	
13	| Route | Status |
14	|---|---|
15	| Native schematic (`${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_sch`) with six measured edit kinds: value, add part, remove part, footprint, reorder, no edit | Supported. See `references/native-edit.md`. |
16	| SKiDL generated schematic | Refused. `source.skidl_unsupported`, exit 2. |
17	| Netlist import, IPC API, pcbnew updater | Not used. `pcbnew` only reads the board. |
18	| GUI update adapter (`update --adapter gui`) | Supported only for the measured image IDs (KiCad 10.0.5, one measured dialog layout). Another image ID is refused. See `references/gui-update.md`. |
19	
20	Open limits: one measured fixture, one machine, KiCad 10.0.5 only, no supplier qualification, no zone refill inside a GUI update.
21	
22	## Procedure
23	
24	1. Read `references/design-workflow.md`. It lists the decisions and the check that closes each one.
25	2. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py env --project PROJECT`. Stop if the report does not show the lock image.
26	3. Edit the schematic as described in `references/native-edit.md`. Write the expected-difference file before the edit.
27	4. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py erc --project PROJECT`. Repair each unwaived violation.
28	5. Update the board from the schematic with `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project PROJECT --adapter gui --expect FILE`. `FILE` is the identity expectation that you wrote before the edit (see `references/gui-update.md`). Use the manual route for any other board edit, and follow `references/placement-routing.md`.
29	6. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py drc --project PROJECT` (add `--refill-zones` to refill the zones and save the board).
30	7. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py sim --project PROJECT` when `${PROJECT}/simulations/` exists.
31	8. After a board change that the wrapper made, run `uv run scripts/pcb.py interface --project PROJECT --apply --expect EXPECT`. `EXPECT` is the expectation of that operation: `${PROJECT}/out/reports/update.expect.json` (GUI update), `${PROJECT}/out/reports/settings.expect.json` (settings) or `${PROJECT}/out/reports/refill.expect.json` (refill). Otherwise record a review with `interface --record-review`.
32	9. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py export --project PROJECT` after clean ERC and DRC results.
33	10. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py check --project PROJECT --for ready`. Report the exit code and the state. Run `check --for export` after an export to compare the published files with their bound hashes. A refused run keeps its logs under `${PROJECT}/out/history/failures/`. A residual staging directory is listed as information.
34	
35	Run every command from the skill directory, or give the absolute path to `scripts/pcb.py`.
36	
37	## Rules for the agent
38	
39	- Never edit a hash by hand, for example `board_sha256` in `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json` or a waiver hash. A hand edit gives an `interface.review_stale` or `interface.geometry_stale` finding (exit 1). Run the command that owns the hash instead.
40	- Before you edit `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_pcb` by hand, run `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project ${PROJECT} --adapter manual`. It preserves the prior board. It exits 2 by design. Then edit the board. Without the preserved board, the rebinding of the interface is refused.
41	
42	- Keep the symbol UUID and the `instances` path of each existing symbol. Never delete and re-add a part to change it.
43	- Change a footprint only through its `Footprint` property.
44	- Never move a symbol to another sheet. The identity is lost.
45	- A board change makes every ERC waiver stale. No operation renews a waiver. The user must renew the waivers.
46	- A GUI save by the user has no prior copy. The rebinding of the interface is then refused. Use the review record.
47	- Do not claim that a board is ready when `check --for ready` exits 1.
48	- Do not claim an identity-kept change when the identity comparison shows an unexpected difference.
49	
50	## Records
51	
52	The validators are separate:
53	
54	- `scripts/validate.py --schemas contracts/schemas --project PROJECT` checks the registry records of the project: `board.yaml`, `variants.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/supplier.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/export.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/waivers.yaml`, `toolchain.lock.json` and `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json`. It also checks the relations between them and the hashes of the board and the schematic. It does not check `${PROJECT}/mechanical/interface-review.json` or `${PROJECT}/components/*.yaml`.
55	- `pcb.py check` runs `validate.py` on each part record in `${PROJECT}/components/*.yaml`, one file at a time. Its readiness check reads `${PROJECT}/mechanical/interface-review.json` (a skill record outside the registry, see `references/design-workflow.md`).
56	- The schemas are in `contracts/schemas/`.
57	
58	## Waivers
59	
60	A waiver lists the exact KiCad item UUIDs of one finding. The set of UUIDs must equal the set of the finding. A label is for display only. A UUID that occurs two times in the project cannot be waived. A waiver for another board or revision is stale and fails the check.
61	
62	## Exit codes
63	
64	See `references/exit-codes.md`. The precedence is 3, then 2, then 1, then 0.
65	
66	## Runtime
67	
68	See `references/runtime.md`. The option `--runtime auto|container|native` selects the route, with `auto` as the default. The native route runs the same tools without podman. It is tested inside the runtime image only, and it checks each operation's own tools and the lock versions. `auto` follows `toolchain.lock.json`, and nothing falls back silently. A conflicting explicit runtime exits 2. `native` is refused on this host (`runtime.native_unavailable`, exit 2): KiCad and pcbnew are not installed outside the image, so the native route is not measured. The lock names the image and its ID. A different ID is a refusal.
69	
70	## Files
71	
72	- `scripts/pcb.py`: the commands.
73	- `scripts/board_inventory.py`: the pcbnew worker that reads holes and placement in the container.
74	- `scripts/validate.py`, `scripts/project_io.py`, `scripts/identity.py`, `scripts/sexp.py`: accepted helpers. They are copies and do not change.
75	- `contracts/`: the record schemas and the copy of their README.
76	- `runtime/`: the fixed build recipe.
77	- `templates/rc-bare-board/`: a bare RC board project.
78	- `examples/rc-edit/`: one value edit with its before files, after files and expected difference.

---
name: pcb-design
description: Edit a KiCad 10 board project with native schematic edits, check it with ERC, DRC, simulation and export checks, and prepare a neutral manufacturing export. Use for RC and small bare-board designs. Not for SKiDL circuits.
---

# pcb-design

This skill guides an agent through a KiCad board design. The agent designs and edits the circuit.
The script `scripts/pcb.py` checks the project and runs the tools. The script never designs a circuit.

## Scope

| Route | Status |
|---|---|
| Native schematic (`${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_sch`) with six measured edit kinds: value, add part, remove part, footprint, reorder, no edit | Supported. See `references/native-edit.md`. |
| SKiDL generated schematic | Refused. `source.skidl_unsupported`, exit 2. |
| Netlist import, IPC API, pcbnew updater | Not used. `pcbnew` only reads the board. |
| GUI update adapter (`update --adapter gui`) | Supported only for the measured image IDs (KiCad 10.0.5, one measured dialog layout). Another image ID is refused. See `references/gui-update.md`. |

Open limits: one measured fixture, one machine, KiCad 10.0.5 only, no supplier qualification, no zone refill inside a GUI update.

## Procedure

1. Read `references/design-workflow.md`. It lists the decisions and the check that closes each one.
2. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py env --project PROJECT`. Stop if the report does not show the lock image.
3. Edit the schematic as described in `references/native-edit.md`. Write the expected-difference file before the edit.
4. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py erc --project PROJECT`. Repair each unwaived violation.
5. Update the board from the schematic with `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project PROJECT --adapter gui --expect FILE`. `FILE` is the identity expectation that you wrote before the edit (see `references/gui-update.md`). Use the manual route for any other board edit, and follow `references/placement-routing.md`.
6. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py drc --project PROJECT` (add `--refill-zones` to refill the zones and save the board).
7. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py sim --project PROJECT` when `${PROJECT}/simulations/` exists.
8. After a board change that the wrapper made, run `uv run scripts/pcb.py interface --project PROJECT --apply --expect EXPECT`. `EXPECT` is the expectation of that operation: `${PROJECT}/out/reports/update.expect.json` (GUI update), `${PROJECT}/out/reports/settings.expect.json` (settings) or `${PROJECT}/out/reports/refill.expect.json` (refill). Otherwise record a review with `interface --record-review`.
9. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py export --project PROJECT` after clean ERC and DRC results.
10. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py check --project PROJECT --for ready`. Report the exit code and the state. Run `check --for export` after an export to compare the published files with their bound hashes. A refused run keeps its logs under `${PROJECT}/out/history/failures/`. A residual staging directory is listed as information.

Run every command from the skill directory, or give the absolute path to `scripts/pcb.py`.

## Rules for the agent

- Never edit a hash by hand, for example `board_sha256` in `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json` or a waiver hash. A hand edit gives an `interface.review_stale` or `interface.geometry_stale` finding (exit 1). Run the command that owns the hash instead.
- Before you edit `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_pcb` by hand, run `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project ${PROJECT} --adapter manual`. It preserves the prior board. It exits 2 by design. Then edit the board. Without the preserved board, the rebinding of the interface is refused.

- Keep the symbol UUID and the `instances` path of each existing symbol. Never delete and re-add a part to change it.
- Change a footprint only through its `Footprint` property.
- Never move a symbol to another sheet. The identity is lost.
- A board change makes every ERC waiver stale. No operation renews a waiver. The user must renew the waivers.
- A GUI save by the user has no prior copy. The rebinding of the interface is then refused. Use the review record.
- Do not claim that a board is ready when `check --for ready` exits 1.
- Do not claim an identity-kept change when the identity comparison shows an unexpected difference.

## Records

The validators are separate:

- `scripts/validate.py --schemas contracts/schemas --project PROJECT` checks the registry records of the project: `board.yaml`, `variants.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/supplier.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/export.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/waivers.yaml`, `toolchain.lock.json` and `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json`. It also checks the relations between them and the hashes of the board and the schematic. It does not check `${PROJECT}/mechanical/interface-review.json` or `${PROJECT}/components/*.yaml`.
- `pcb.py check` runs `validate.py` on each part record in `${PROJECT}/components/*.yaml`, one file at a time. Its readiness check reads `${PROJECT}/mechanical/interface-review.json` (a skill record outside the registry, see `references/design-workflow.md`).
- The schemas are in `contracts/schemas/`.

## Waivers

A waiver lists the exact KiCad item UUIDs of one finding. The set of UUIDs must equal the set of the finding. A label is for display only. A UUID that occurs two times in the project cannot be waived. A waiver for another board or revision is stale and fails the check.

## Exit codes

See `references/exit-codes.md`. The precedence is 3, then 2, then 1, then 0.

## Runtime

See `references/runtime.md`. The option `--runtime auto|container|native` selects the route, with `auto` as the default. The native route runs the same tools without podman. It is tested inside the runtime image only, and it checks each operation's own tools and the lock versions. `auto` follows `toolchain.lock.json`, and nothing falls back silently. A conflicting explicit runtime exits 2. `native` is refused on this host (`runtime.native_unavailable`, exit 2): KiCad and pcbnew are not installed outside the image, so the native route is not measured. The lock names the image and its ID. A different ID is a refusal.

## Files

- `scripts/pcb.py`: the commands.
- `scripts/board_inventory.py`: the pcbnew worker that reads holes and placement in the container.
- `scripts/validate.py`, `scripts/project_io.py`, `scripts/identity.py`, `scripts/sexp.py`: accepted helpers. They are copies and do not change.
- `contracts/`: the record schemas and the copy of their README.
- `runtime/`: the fixed build recipe.
- `templates/rc-bare-board/`: a bare RC board project.
- `examples/rc-edit/`: one value edit with its before files, after files and expected difference.
